doc.title: Junior Mance Part II interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 18, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]

title: The wristwatch alarm going off during jury duty
summary: He tells how his watch alarm went off in court during jury duty.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Yeah. So I want to really get into that. I might use it more like for the classroom work. Anytime I want to do parts I can do them, and play them and they’ll come out. So that’s the only reason I bought it, just to use as a midi. I was going to tell you about this watch. Last year I was doing jury duty. You know and with jury duty you have to get there early on occasion. And I’m not an early morning person at all. So I’m leaning on my hands and I’m falling asleep, so after a while this thing goes off, and it’s quiet in the room, it’s like between the district attorney questioning the person. And everybody stops. And so I happened to open my eyes, because the quiet will wake you more than noise will. And the judge is looking around and he looked at the clock, and the clock said exactly what my watch said, twelve o’clock. And so the lady sitting next to me, she touched me and she said, “I think that’s you.” And then I said, “Oh my goodness” and I shut it off, and I said, “Sorry, your honor.” And even he got a kick out of it. He says, “It’s lunch time anyway, recess.” So I think the rest of the jury, were also glad that my thing went off. I know I was because I was finding it hard to stay awake. And it was a boring case and they do give you recesses if they find you are like really getting bored or sleepy and tired. They want you fresh all the time. So we took a lunch break. But it was embarrassing. You know I woke up and the whole courtroom, they’re looking right at me like I’m on trial or something.
The judge smiles and cracked a laugh. I said, “Sorry about that.” So the next day I wore a different watch, I should have worn it today.
